inline_comments.comment: This type-only import crosses a package boundary — core-server reaching into the React renderer's source tree via a five-level relative path (`../../../../../renderers/react/src/...`). While `import type` creates no runtime coupling, it creates a hard structural dependency: renaming or moving `componentMetaExtractor.ts` in the renderer silently breaks the core build. The comment acknowledges this but the design is still fragile. A better approach would be to define a shared interface (e.g. `ComponentDoc`) in the `storybook/internal/types` package that both the core manifest renderer and the React renderer implement, keeping the dependency direction clean.

The `type` field is mapped as `prop.type?.raw ?? prop.type?.name`, which produces `string | undefined`. However, `ParsedDocgen.props` is typed as `Record<string, PropItem>` (imported from `react-docgen-typescript`), where `PropItem.type` is `PropItemType` — an object with shape `{ name: string; raw?: string; value?: EnumValue[] }`, not a plain string. This is a structural type mismatch. At runtime, any downstream code that calls `type.name` on a parsed react-component-meta prop will receive `undefined` (since strings do not have a `.name` property), silently producing empty type displays in the debugger UI. The fix is to wrap the value: `type: { name: prop.type?.raw ?? prop.type?.name ?? '' }`.

The `while (candidate !== path.dirname(candidate))` loop in `watchProgramSourceDirs` has no depth limit. On a project where no `package.json` or `tsconfig.json` is found along the walk (e.g. a stray source file or an unusual monorepo layout), this loop will walk all the way to the filesystem root for every unique source directory. The `checker/ComponentMetaManager.ts` — the implementation actually used by the generator — correctly applies `const MAX_WALK_DEPTH = 10` with `&& depth < MAX_WALK_DEPTH` in this same loop. This file should apply the same guard.

The module-level `componentMetaManager` singleton is never disposed between invocations. `createComponentMetaManager` only caches the manager when `watch` is `true` and reuses it on subsequent calls. However, if the Storybook dev server undergoes a full restart while the module remains loaded (e.g. via hot-module replacement or a second `manifests()` call after config changes), the previous manager — which may hold active `FSWatcher` instances and TypeScript `LanguageService` objects — is silently orphaned and never disposed. Consider disposing the old instance when a new one is being created: `componentMetaManager?.dispose(); componentMetaManager = manager;`.

`typescriptOptions.reactDocgen || 'react-docgen'` silently converts an explicit `false` (user-disabled docgen) into `'react-docgen'`. In the previous implementation, `reactDocgen: false` in the TypeScript options was a supported way to disable prop extraction entirely. This change regresses that behaviour: users who opted out of docgen will now have `react-docgen` enabled without warning. The condition should be: `typescriptOptions.reactDocgen !== false ? (typescriptOptions.reactDocgen ?? 'react-docgen') : 'react-docgen'` — or, more clearly, check `reactDocgen === false` upfront and short-circuit.

The empty `catch {}` block swallows all extraction errors without any logging. This makes it impossible to diagnose why a specific component silently produces no props in the manifest. Even a single `logger.debug(...)` call would be valuable: `catch (err) { logger.debug('[reactComponentMeta] extraction failed for ' + entry.storyPath + ': ' + err); }`. The same pattern exists in the `checker/ComponentMetaProject.ts` counterpart and should be addressed there as well.

`docgenEngine` is now a required parameter in `getComponentData`, which is marked `@public` in the JSDoc. This is a breaking API change for any consumer of the `@storybook/react` package that currently calls `getComponentData` without specifying an engine. Before merging, the parameter should either be made optional with a sensible default (e.g. `docgenEngine: DocgenEngine = 'react-docgen'`), or the public-API exposure should be re-evaluated. The same applies to `getComponents`.

`watch` is passed to `presets.apply('experimental_manifests', ...)` as part of the options object. In `writeManifests`, `getManifests(presets)` is called with no second argument, so `watch` will be `undefined` at the call site. However, the `manifests` preset function in `generator.ts` types its options as `{ manifestEntries: IndexEntry[]; watch: boolean }` — non-optional `boolean`. This means `watch: undefined` is silently passed where `boolean` is expected, making the type contract unreliable. Either change the type to `watch?: boolean` in the preset options, or ensure `writeManifests` explicitly passes `{ watch: false }`.

The `--max_old_space_size` for `storybook:ui:build` was silently bumped from 4096 to 5120 MiB. This kind of infrastructure change should be accompanied by a comment or commit message explaining why (presumably the new `@volar/language-core` + `@volar/typescript` dependencies increase the build memory footprint). Without context, future engineers cannot know whether this limit is safe to reduce.

general_comments.comment: There is severe code duplication across three pairs of near-identical files: `checker/ComponentMetaManager.ts` vs `componentMeta/ComponentMetaManager.ts` (~620 lines each), `checker/ComponentMetaProject.ts` vs `componentMeta/ComponentMetaProject.ts` (~465 lines each), and the root-level `componentMetaExtractor.ts` vs `componentMeta/componentMetaExtractor.ts` (~1732 lines each — differing only in relative import paths `./types`/`../types`). This is approximately 5,500 lines of duplicated implementation code. `generator.ts` imports exclusively from `./checker`, meaning the entire `componentMeta/` directory is unreachable production code. It appears `componentMeta/` was an iterative development directory that was accidentally committed alongside the final `checker/` implementation. The `componentMeta/` directory (and its duplicate extractor) should be removed, and all its test coverage migrated to use the `checker/` classes directly. This will also eliminate the maintenance burden of keeping two implementations in sync — the `MAX_WALK_DEPTH` discrepancy flagged inline is a concrete example of divergence that has already occurred.

The `checker/` and `componentMeta/` directories also contain nearly identical test helpers (`checker/test-helpers.ts` vs `componentMeta/test-helpers.ts`) and large overlapping test suites. For example, `sortTSConfigs`/`isFileInDir` unit tests are duplicated verbatim across `checker/ComponentMetaManager.test.ts` and `componentMeta/ComponentMetaManager.test.ts`. Once the implementation duplication is resolved, the test infrastructure should be consolidated into a single shared helper module so future fixes or additions only need to be made in one place.
